name: Propositum
description: Watches the sources you approve, while a work session is running. Nothing else.
_comment_permissions: Every permission here is WARNING-FREE at install. Chrome shows no scary
prompt for any of them, which matters because a consumer product that asks
to 'read your browsing history' has already lost the argument it is trying
to make.
DELIBERATELY ABSENT — see ADR-0002:
tabs          would grant the URL and title of EVERY tab. Without it the
extension is structurally incapable of learning the person
visited anything they did not approve. Chrome enforces the
constraint, not our code.
webNavigation costs the 'Read your browsing history' warning, and carries
transitionType — the most semantically loaded signal there
is ('typed it' vs 'followed a link'). We give it up and take
document.referrer plus Navigation Timing as partial
substitutes. Revisit only if H1 scores badly and ablation
points here.
history       not needed and not defensible.
debugger      would make every constraint below advisory.
notifications is warning-free and is the ONLY way to surface an offer
nobody asked for. sidePanel.open() requires a user gesture, so calling it
from an alarm silently throws — which is exactly what happened: the app
named the subject correctly and the person saw nothing but a small dot.
_comment_hosts: BROAD BY DECISION, and this reverses ADR-0002. Detection cannot work on
sources the person has not set up yet, and the whole point of the feature
is noticing work before they have told us about it. That costs Chrome's
'Read and change all your data on all websites' warning at install, which
is the honest price and is not hidden anywhere in the UI.
What limits the exposure is NOT the permission any more, so it has to be
the behaviour, and it is enforced in two places:
- content.js sends METADATA ONLY while no session is running: a cleaned
URL, a title, dwell and scroll. Never page text.
- the app holds those in memory, bounded and discarded, and they never
reach the ledger unless the person accepts an offer.
Full page text still begins only after a session starts on an approved
_comment_loopback: The app's own origin, and the ONLY entry here that is not warning-free.
A service worker fetch to http://127.0.0.1 is cross-origin, and the app
sends no CORS headers deliberately — CORS protects nothing on loopback,
which is why the transport has four controls of its own. Without this the
extension cannot reach the app at all: the health check fails, the badge
shows '!', and capture is silently OFF.
Pinned to the port in package.json's dev script; a test asserts they match.
_comment_key: Pinned so the extension id is stable. Without it the id changes if the repo
moves, and the Origin check on the loopback transport starts rejecting our
REPLACE before any real install — this is a placeholder.
